_note: Baseline. Every other row in this file renders similarly and compares unequal.
Right-to-left mark. Invisible; reorders everything after it in a rendered report.
Right-to-left override - the trojan-source character. Invisible AND it inverts display order, so a label can render as something it is not.
Zero-width joiner outside any emoji sequence.
Zero-width space. Breaks an exact-match join with ascii_control while rendering identically to it.
No-break space where U+0020 is expected. An ASCII-only trim leaves it in place.
Soft hyphen. Invisible unless the renderer decides to break the line there.

A byte-order mark that leaked into the FIELD - the file itself has none. The classic result of concatenating UTF-8-with-BOM exports; it makes only the first column of the first row unequal, so it survives most spot checks.
Cyrillic A, es and ie substituted for Latin A, c and e. Renders as `Acme`, joins to nothing. The homoglyph specimen.
Fullwidth digits one-two-three. Digit-valued to Unicode, uncastable to any numeric type - see numerics.csv arabic_indic_digits for the same problem in a numeric field.
Arabic-Indic digits one-two-three as an identity string rather than an amount.
Precomposed e-acute. Byte-unequal to nfd_form and canonically equivalent to it.

Decomposed e-acute. Equal to nfc_form under NFC, unequal byte-wise - so dedupe, `unique` and every join disagree with a human reading the two rows. THE normalization specimen; a `length` rule also disagrees (4 vs 5).
A single astral-plane codepoint (factory). One codepoint, two UTF-16 code units, four UTF-8 bytes - so `length` means three different numbers depending on the engine.
One grapheme cluster, three codepoints, eleven UTF-8 bytes. Truncating it by codepoint or by byte produces a different emoji or mojibake.
One grapheme, thirteen codepoints. The upper-bound case for any `length` rule.
A combining acute with no base character. It renders attached to whatever precedes it - including a delimiter or a quote in a report.

A lone surrogate is not expressible in UTF-8, so it CANNOT appear literally in this file. What production actually delivers is this six-character ESCAPE SEQUENCE inside a JSON string, which is the form a JSONPath extract has to survive. That is the specimen; a suite wanting the raw ill-formed bytes must synthesize them in code.
U+FFFD - a decode already failed upstream. The original bytes are gone, so only quarantining or flagging the row preserves any chance of a re-fetch.
A horizontal tab inside a CSV field. Harmless here, fatal to a TSV re-export.
Unquoted empty - NULL, for the same D19 reason as every other file's empty_field.
Quoted empty - the empty STRING. Renders identically to empty_field and is a different value; `length` fires on this one, `not_null` on the other.
